skill.name: building-nextjs-apps
skill.description: Guides creation and migration of Next.js 16 applications using App Router patterns, async route parameters, proxy.ts, Turbopack, cache components, and focused frontend design guidance.
skill.summary: Build and upgrade Next.js 16 apps with current routing, data fetching, proxy, and design patterns.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code formatting, JavaScript template literals, placeholder URLs, and documented Next.js examples. No prompt-injection attempt or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found. One medium semantic risk remains because the skill recommends running an unpinned third-party MCP package through npx.

remediation.issue: Unpinned third-party MCP execution through npx
remediation.suggestion: Pin next-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and tell users to inspect the package before enabling it in agent tooling.

remediation.issue: Placeholder network and environment examples can be copied into production
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholder URLs and process.env examples as examples only, and require users to validate destinations and secret handling.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned MCP Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends configuring next-devtools MCP through npx with @latest, which can execute a changing third-party package during agent use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup block explicitly adds an MCP server with npx next-devtools-mcp@latest and repeats that command in JSON configuration. This is a clear supply-chain risk, although the package appears related to the skill purpose.

content.value_statement: Next.js 16 changed routing, middleware, caching, and build defaults, which can break older project patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance for modern App Router apps and migrations.
actual_capabilities: Shows correct async params and searchParams patterns for pages, layouts, route handlers, and metadata.
Explains the migration from middleware.ts to proxy.ts in Next.js 16 applications.
Provides examples for server components, client components, API routes, server actions, and data fetching.
Covers Turbopack configuration, cacheComponents, image changes, and parallel route defaults.
Includes frontend design guidance for more distinctive React application interfaces.
Documents datetime-local conversion patterns for UTC storage and local display.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not validate generated applications by itself.
Some examples use placeholder URLs and must be adapted before production use.
It focuses on Next.js and React, not non-React frontend frameworks.
Version claims should be checked against current Next.js documentation before major upgrades.

use_cases.title: Start a New App
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js 16 project with App Router layouts, routes, data fetching, and UI structure from the beginning.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an Existing Project
use_cases.description: Move a Next.js 15 project toward Next.js 16 by updating route params, middleware naming, and configuration patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Implementation Patterns
use_cases.description: Check generated code for common Next.js 16 mistakes before merging or handing it to a team.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small App Router page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a simple Next.js 16 page with a root layout, one route, and correct async params where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dynamic Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dynamic Next.js 16 route for tasks. Use async params, generateMetadata, and a clear loading and not-found flow.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Middleware
prompt_templates.scenario: Migration request from an older project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js project for version 16 migration issues. Focus on proxy.ts, async params, Turbopack, image props, and parallel routes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete product workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Next.js 16 task dashboard with server actions, API routes, authenticated proxy behavior, UTC datetime handling, and polished frontend design.

output_examples.input: Create a dynamic task detail page for Next.js 16.
output: A route plan that awaits params before reading the task id.
A metadata approach that handles missing records cleanly.
A not-found path and page structure suitable for App Router.

output_examples.input: Upgrade this app from Next.js 15 patterns.
output: A checklist for async params, searchParams, route handlers, and metadata.
A migration note for replacing middleware.ts with proxy.ts.
Configuration guidance for Turbopack and cacheComponents.

output_examples.input: Improve the frontend quality of a generated dashboard.
output: A clearer visual direction for typography, spacing, color, and motion.
Component-level guidance that keeps the interface usable and distinctive.
Notes about avoiding generic layouts and placeholder-heavy design.

best_practices: Ask for the target Next.js version and project structure before applying migration advice.
Validate external URLs, environment variables, and authentication flows before production deployment.
Run type checks, linting, and a local build after applying generated changes.
anti_patterns: Do not read params or searchParams synchronously in Next.js 16 routes.
Do not keep middleware.ts when the project expects the Next.js 16 proxy.ts convention.
Do not copy placeholder API URLs, tokens, or script sources into production without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build and migrate Next.js 16 applications with App Router, route handlers, data fetching, and frontend design guidance.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready security code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples. Authentication, secrets, and proxy behavior still need project-specific review.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from Next.js 15?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights async params, proxy.ts, Turbopack defaults, cacheComponents, image changes, and parallel route defaults.

faq.question: Does it require a specific UI library?
faq.answer: No. It mentions common setup patterns, but the design guidance can be adapted to different component systems.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify after applying it?
faq.answer: Users should run linting, type checks, builds, and manual tests for routing, authentication, and data loading.
